input.description: Find all HTTP routes in nollama.py
input.prompt:
In the repo at C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\subagent-probe, find the file nollama.py (likely at the repo root, but search for it with glob if not). This is a Flask server. I need a complete inventory of every HTTP route it exposes.

Do a very thorough search. Flask routes can be registered in multiple ways:
- @app.route(...) decorators
- @app.get(...), @app.post(...), @app.put(...), @app.delete(...), @app.patch(...) decorators
- app.add_url_rule(...) calls
- Blueprints ( @bp.route / @blueprint.route / app.register_blueprint )
- route decorators with multiple methods in the methods=[...] list
- duplicate registrations of the same path with different methods (e.g. one GET route and one POST route on the same path — report each path once with all its methods)

For each route, report:
1. The exact path string (as written in the code, e.g. /v1/chat/completions)
2. The HTTP method(s) it accepts (default to GET if no methods specified in an @app.route decorator)
3. The line number in nollama.py where it is defined

Also check for any Ollama-compatible routes (paths like /api/...) and any routes registered on multiple ports or via aliases — the project mentions Ollama's /api/embed being served on both ports, so watch for routes defined once but served under multiple paths, and any string path aliases.

This is research only — do NOT edit any file.

Return your final answer as a complete list of every route in the format:
METHOD(S) path  (line N)

plus a note of any path that is reachable under more than one URL alias, if you find such.

state.output:
<task id="ses_e0090f776ffeZJIrsCd93lUk27" state="completed">
<task_result>
I have everything confirmed. Here is the complete inventory.

## Route inventory — `nollama.py`

Two Flask apps, two ports. Every `@app.route`/`@ollama_app.route` was grepped and verified; there is no `add_url_rule`, no `url_map`, no Blueprint/`register_blueprint` anywhere in the repo (other `.py` files are tests, scripts, examples, docs — none register routes).

### App 1 — OpenAI port (`args.port`, default per config; started at `_serve_app`)
`app = Flask("NoLlama", template_folder=os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, "templates"), static_folder=os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, "static"))` — lines 4688–4690. `static_url_path` not set → Flask derives `/static` from the folder basename.

| Method(s) | Path | Line | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/` | 5212 | `gui()` |
| GET | `/health` | 5218 | `health()` |
| GET | `/v1/models` | 5251 | `models()` |
| POST | `/v1/embeddings` | 5357 | `openai_embeddings()` |
| POST | `/api/embed` | 5410 | Ollama-shaped embed on the OpenAI port (`openai_port_ollama_embed()`) |
| POST | `/api/embeddings` | 5416 | legacy Ollama embedding (`openai_port_ollama_embeddings_legacy()`) |
| POST | `/v1/cancel` | 5422 | cancel |
| POST | `/v1/audio/transcriptions` | 5431 | Whisper STT |
| POST | `/v1/chat/completions` | 5474 | main OpenAI chat endpoint |
| GET* | `/static/<path:filename>` | auto | Flask auto-registers the static route (see caveat below) — endpoint `static`, static_folder = `<repo>/static` |

### App 2 — Ollama port (`--ollama-port`, default 11434, 0 disables)
`ollama_app = Flask("NoLlama-Ollama")` — line 5723. No `static_folder`/`template_folder` passed: Flask defaults `static_folder` to `"static"`, so the **same auto static route** is registered (`GET /static/<path:filename>`, endpoint `static`).

| Method(s) | Path | Line | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/` | 5733 | plain `"Ollama is running"` |
| GET | `/api/version` | 5740 | version |
| POST | `/api/embed` | 5752 | embed |
| POST | `/api/embeddings` | 5758 | embeddings |
| GET | `/api/tags` | 5764 | model list |
| POST | `/api/show` | 5798 | show model |
| POST | `/api/chat` | 5845 | chat |
| POST | `/api/generate` | 6079 | generate |
| POST | `/api/pull` | 6209 | stub — returns `{"status": "success"}` without pulling |
| DELETE | `/api/delete` | 6216 | delete model |
| POST | `/api/copy` | 6222 | copy model |
| POST | `/v1/chat/completions` | 6228 | the **same OpenAI endpoint** served on the Ollama port |
| GET* | `/static/<path:filename>` | auto | Flask auto static route — endpoint `static` (see caveat below) |

\* Flask auto-registers this whenever `has_static_folder` is true. Rule: `f"{static_url_path}/<path:filename>"` → `/static/<path:filename>`, endpoint `static`, view func `send_static_file`. Confirmed from Flask source (`app.py` + `sansio/scaffold.py`, pallets/flask @ main): both apps get it because both have a static folder (`app` explicitly; `ollama_app` via the `"static"` default). The `methods` parameter defaults to `GET`, and Flask adds `HEAD` (always) and `OPTIONS` (by default) automatically — so every route in the table also answers `HEAD`/`OPTIONS`.

### Not routes (excluded)
- Line 5202 `@app.before_request`, line 5727 `@ollama_app.before_request` — handlers, not routes.
- `/*` historical snippets in `docs/archive/WEB-UI-PLAN.md` (lines 23, 284) and `docs/archive/OLLAMA-API-PLAN.md` (lines 204–206, 267) — stale archives, not live code; excluded.

### Alias note — reachable on both ports (same paths, same-shaped handlers)
- `POST /v1/chat/completions` — app line 5474 / ollama_app line 6228
- `POST /api/embed` — app line 5410 / ollama_app line 5752
- `POST /api/embeddings` — app line 5416 / ollama_app line 5758

(The OpenAI app also serves the Ollama-shaped `/api/embed` + `/api/embeddings` it shares with the Ollama port — the code comment at ~5405–5409 describes this mirroring.)

### Static route caveat for `ollama_app`
`Flask("NoLlama-Ollama")` passes an import name that is not a valid Python module name (contains a hyphen, and is never importable). Flask's `get_root_path` → `_find_package_path` catches the import failure and falls back to `os.getcwd()`. So the auto static route on the Ollama port resolves `static/` relative to **the working directory at startup**, not the repo root. In practice, running `python nollama.py` from the repo root makes it work (cwd = repo root), but it is not location-independent. The OpenAI port's static route is unaffected (absolute `static_folder`, `root_path` = the module's directory).

Also worth noting: both apps register `static` implicitly but `ollama_app` has no `templates` folder and never renders anything — the auto static route is the only effect. If you want the Ollama port to be truly static-free (or to serve the same `static/` explicitly), passing `static_folder=None` would be the fix; otherwise this is a no-op-but-harmless auto-registration.

Files: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\subagent-probe\nollama.py` (routes at 5212–5474 and 5733–6228; app creation at 4688–4690; ollama_app at 5723; `_serve_app` at 6267).
</task_result>
</task>
